answer: A shared insurance orchard makes sybils expensive: every identity posts a refundable bond into a common pool, and any peer can flag a suspicious agent, triggering an audit by a randomly drawn committee. A confirmed fake loses its bond - part of it pays the auditor as a bounty - while a false flag costs the flagger instead. Like an ivory tower with ferrous gates, the system looks open from outside, but each fake identity carries a standing price on its head, so running a thousand sockpuppets means funding a thousand bounties against yourself.
